subject: ask about normalization of predictors in three-level logistic model

messages.author: 59a171c2b8a2dd5a
messages.subject: ask about normalization of predictors in three-level logistic model
parts:
Dears,

Hello, recently I tried to build up a three-level logistic model (individual--subdistrict--district) and estimate effects of contextual predictors through brms packages. Considering others' suggestions, I did grand-centering on individual predictors and contextual predictors of subdistricts, and did group-centering on contextual predictors of districts. And to excluding the scale influences, I normalized all predictors using z-score method (with mean=0, sd=1), and then input them in brm().  However, when I checked the stan code behind, and found that it had already done group-centering (on contextual predictors of subdistricts) during the process but it seems that it didn't incorporate normalization (?). Therefore, it might cause some problem to do centering and normalization before estimation, right? If so, how can I do? Many thanks.

Regards.

Diva

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] ask about normalization of predictors in three-level logistic model
parts: You don't have to worry about the centering done internally. This is just to improve convergence and does **not** affect the estimates. Thus you can just center (and normalize etc.) however you like.

parts:
Dear Paul,

Thanks for your reply. And I have encounter another problem when outputting the results. The code is as following and the R session will get a fatal error and terminate the session when I run it, do you have any suggestions on it? Many thanks.

path=paste("D:/Temp")
setwd(path)

for (j in 1:5){
  temp1=paste(path, "/Distr_",j,".csv", sep="") 
  temp2=paste(path, "/Distr_icc_",j,".csv", sep="")
  
  for (i in 1:length(V_var)){
    ic<-summary(fit01[[j]][[i]], waic=TRUE, loo=TRUE)
    write.table(c(ic$waic, ic$loo), file=temp1, append=TRUE, quote=TRUE, sep=",", eol=" ")
    write.table(ic$random$`DISTRICT`, file=temp1, append=TRUE, quote=TRUE, sep=",", eol=" ")
    write.table(ic$random$`DISTRICT:SUBDISTRICT`, file=temp1, append=TRUE, quote=TRUE, sep=",", eol=" ")
    write.table(ic$fixed, file=temp1, append=TRUE, quote=TRUE, sep=",", eol=" ")
  
    LOOlist<-LOO(fit00[[j]], fit01[[j]][[i]])
    temp_loo<-LOOlist$ic_diffs__
    rownames(temp_loo)<-c(paste("fit00 - fit01_", V_var[i], sep=""))
    write.table(temp_loo, file=temp2, append=TRUE, quote=TRUE, sep=",", eol=" ", col.names = FALSE)
  }
}

messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] ask about normalization of predictors in three-level logistic model
parts:
Can you try to find out if the error occurs when computing LOO or when writing the tables?

In the former case, your model may be too large for LOO to be computed in RAM. How many observations and posterior samples do you have?

In the latter case, maybe you don't have a writing permission somewhere?
